transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-02-28 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Lena, Tom, Priya, Marcus, Olivia, James, Nora, Evan, Sofia

Auto-generated Summary (brief):
- Quick sync across IT, Finance Ops, Security and Audit on SOC2 evidence gaps, infra cost controls (Dedicated vs Hosted), and an upcoming bench test for private quantized model runs. Decided owners for artifact updates and a short performance run in a private VPC.

Topics: SOC2 artifacts, KMS key handling, cost comparison (Dedicated/reserved vs hosted on-demand), network peering checklist, bench test scheduling, procurement timing.

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: all right, hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. I think we have about 45 minutes, um, I want to run through the SOC2 evidence map first and then the infra cost questions — keep it tight.
[00:35] Tom Alvarez: yeah, sounds good. I threw up a quick runbook link in the chat, the network peering checklist, but, uh, it's still rough.
[00:50] Priya Nair: perfect. Also I flagged a couple of open items for audit - rotation of KMS keys and service account inventory.
[01:05] Marcus Chen: from finance side we've got the Q2 forecast and a couple of reserve options to discuss — committed capacity versus on-demand. We'll need to show the delta to procurement.
[01:25] Nora Patel: just to note procurement timeline — if we go for reserved Dedicated GPUs, procurement lead times are about 4-6 weeks, plus approvals.
[01:40] James Li: legal's review on vendor TOC and DPA comments is mostly done, but we need the SOC2 scoping doc updated to reflect the Dedicated-enclave option.
[02:05] Lena Ortiz: okay, Priya, can you walk us briefly through the KMS/HSM ask? I want to make sure everyone hears the risk impact.
[02:22] Priya Nair: sure. So current state: our hosted offering uses cloud KMS with default rotation; for Private we want customer-managed keys or an HSM option. Audit is asking for documented rotation cadence, access logs, and separation of duties. We also need a diagram showing key lifecycle — creation, use, rotate, retire.
[02:45] Evan Brooks: just to add, the runtime needs a short-lived token to mount the key; we're working on automating that. There was a small mismatch last quarter where a service account had broader access than intended — that shows up on the inventory.
[03:10] Sofia Mendes: yep, for SOC2 we need evidence (screenshots/config exports) and a written narrative. The narrative should align with the diagram.
[03:30] Tom Alvarez: question on the bench: are we doing quantized model runs in private or hosted? Latency/cost numbers change a lot depending on that.
[03:45] Olivia Park: we recommended doing it in Private for fidelity — we can repro a customer's VPC setup. Also quantized kernels sometimes behave differently on on-prem hardware.
[04:05] Marcus Chen: if we do it on Dedicated reserved capacity, cost per token goes down in long run, but we have commit risk. I'll model three scenarios: on-demand hosted, reserved Dedicated 6-month, and burst Dedicated with on-demand bun- — bunk? (laughter) — sorry burst.
[04:30] Lena Ortiz: notes: Marcus will share the delta numbers.

[06:10] (transcription glitch) Speaker 2: uh-huh, mm-hmm.

[06:28] Priya Nair: another item — RBAC for admin operations: audit wants role separation across infra, security, and finance. We need a mapping of who has keys to what and change approval flow.
[06:48] James Li: we can accept a ticketing audit trail from ServiceNow as evidence if it captures approvals and times.
[07:05] Nora Patel: procurement can provide PO timelines and vendor intake forms. I'll attach the supplier questionnaire.

[09:00] Tom Alvarez: network side — peering is straightforward but we need: static route docs, egress filtering, and a playbook for peering failover. Also, for Private deployments we've seen MTU issues with VPN appliances.
[09:25] Evan Brooks: should we standardize on IP ranges for test vpcs? Means less friction when we spin up bench clusters.
[09:45] Lena Ortiz: yes please, make a template. Evan, can you do that?
[10:01] Evan Brooks: yep, I'll post a template and a small runbook.

[11:20] Marcus Chen: quick finance note — for Q2 pilots we need to know expected hours of GPU usage per week. If you give me an estimate I can map to cost under each procurement scenario.
[11:42] Olivia Park: I'll give you a baseline — we have a rough perf profile for the T4 and A10 equivalent tests; but quantized A10s might do 2.5x throughput per GPU, so that changes math.
[12:05] Marcus Chen: cool. Also, small ask — can we tag bench runs with project codes for chargeback tracking?
[12:18] Tom Alvarez: yes, we have tagging support, but we need to ensure the scheduler propagates tags to the billing export. That's on me.

[14:30] (background cross-talk) Speaker 3: yeah, sorry, go ahead.

[14:50] Priya Nair: on evidence items: I'm missing the last three KMS rotation logs and proof of key deletion procedures for decomposed tenants. Can infra pull those?
[15:10] Tom Alvarez: I think we have logs but might need a script to export the exact fields audit expects. I'll work with Olivia to produce the export.
[15:35] James Li: note: legal wants any third-party subprocessor list updated if we route logs to external monitoring.
[15:55] Lena Ortiz: good catch. We'll list external telemetry providers.

[17:10] (small gap)

[17:40] Marcus Chen: procurement pricing note — if we commit to 12 months on Dedicated we could get deeper discounts, but it's only worth it if utilization > 60%. Otherwise on-demand and burst is cheaper. I'll include utilization scenarios.
[18:02] Nora Patel: procurement will need approval packages if >$200k commit. Also vendor risk gets escalated for HSM vendors.
[18:20] Priya Nair: for HSMs, audit wants key ceremony documentation (even if virtual) and attestation. We should aim to use a FedRAMP/ISO-certified HSM provider or document compensating controls.

[20:00] Olivia Park: small dev-tools ask — can infra expose an API to create bench clusters with proper tags and ephemeral keys? That'd make the bench runs reproducible.
[20:20] Evan Brooks: yeah, we can add a lambda that provisions ephemeral creds; security review needed.
[20:50] Lena Ortiz: okay, looks like action items forming.

[22:10] (transcription artifact: 'KV cache' heard as 'kayvee cache')

[22:30] Tom Alvarez: important: if we use prefix caching or KV cache for inference, we need to capture cache eviction logs for debugging; audit sometimes asks for evidence of data retention in caches. That's a bit tricky.
[22:55] Priya Nair: agreed. We should document TTLs and retention policies. If any cached data is PII, it must be encrypted at rest with key rotation aligned.
[23:20] Marcus Chen: also, cost-wise cache can reduce token compute by about 15% on average for our LLM workloads — I'll model that impact as well.

[25:00] Sofia Mendes: one ask from audit — a short narrative describing fallback policies: e.g., if Dedicated capacity is exhausted, does traffic go to hosted or degrade gracefully? We need that written and an example incident flow.
[25:30] Tom Alvarez: we do have automated fallback rules in the router; I'll extract configuration and example logs.
[25:55] Lena Ortiz: can you include an SLA map for that fallback? I want the doc to show our intended customer experience.
[26:20] Tom Alvarez: yes I'll add latency tiers and fallback path.

[28:00] (brief pause)

[28:20] Priya Nair: on the SSO front: audit wants last-login logs and a recent SAML metadata export. James, is legal okay with us providing the SAML metadata to auditors?
[28:35] James Li: yes, as long as it's internal metadata and we redact any cert private material. We should provide only public metadata and logs with PII redacted.
[28:50] Nora Patel: procurement needs to confirm that any onboarding paperwork doesn't force long-term lock-in for the HSM vendor.

[30:10] Marcus Chen: timeline check — if we want procurement to get a PO in place by mid-April for a May pilot, we need final numbers by early March. That align?
[30:30] Lena Ortiz: yes — Marcus and Tom to finalize cost and bench scope by March 5.

[32:00] Evan Brooks: I'll stand up a small private VPC bench for 2 hours to capture perf numbers; want to do that week of March 9. Who's available?
[32:20] Olivia Park: Dev tools and infra can join; Priya should witness to validate configs.
[32:35] Priya Nair: yep I can join the run.

[34:10] (interruption) Speaker 1: uh, sorry, slow wifi.

[34:40] Tom Alvarez: on the export artifacts — I'm going to produce a single zip with: network peering docs, KMS rotation logs, fallback config snippets, and scheduler tag proof. I'll put a pointer in the drive.
[35:00] Lena Ortiz: perfect. Priya, Sofia, legal — will you review that zip for audit completeness?
[35:12] Sofia Mendes: yes, we'll review and send back comments.

[36:30] Marcus Chen: quick ask — can legal sign off on procurement language for HSM service? We may need a slight amendment for key custody terms.
[36:48] James Li: yes, I can draft a short clause. Need to see the vendor terms first.

[38:00] (crosstalk)

[38:30] Lena Ortiz: any blockers we didn't cover?
[38:40] Nora Patel: timeline risk if vendor takes longer to respond; procurement will push but we might need a fallback vendor.
[39:00] Priya Nair: nothing else from security beyond KMS doc and RBAC map.
[39:15] Tom Alvarez: infra needs a little time to script the KMS export, but no blocker.

[40:20] Lena Ortiz: recap — owners and due dates: Marcus cost model (3 scenarios) due Mar 5; Lena updates SOC2 evidence map Mar 3; Priya KMS rotation plan Mar 10; Tom bench run config and artifact zip by Mar 6; Evan VPC template Mar 6.
[41:05] Olivia Park: I'll add the bench profile to the shared doc and tag it with the project code. Link: https://drive.redwood/ops/bench-profile (note: internal link)

[42:30] James Li: legal will expect a readout before procurement approval; can we put a 30-min legal sign-off on Mar 9?
[42:50] Lena Ortiz: yes let's pencil that in.

[44:00] (closing)

[44:15] Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone. I'll upload the updated scoping sheet and meeting notes later today. If you see anything missing in the action items add it in the doc.
[44:30] Marcus Chen: thanks — I'll kick off the cost model and share.
[44:45] Priya Nair: thanks all.

Conclusion: meeting closed ~15:45 UTC.

References/shared artifacts mentioned:

- SOC2 evidence map (drive)
